subject: CAIQ control lineage appendix and sample playbook
messages:
From: Julie Chen <julie.chen@atlassecurity.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: caiq@atlassecurity.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ - request for control lineage examples and typical artifacts

Hi Tessa / Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking our call earlier. As we start the CAIQ review for Atlas, our assessment team would like a short appendix that maps a handful of high-risk controls (for example: IAM, key management, tenant isolation, logging) to the exact artifact types and where we can retrieve them during sampling.

Specifically we need: 
- A compact "control lineage" CSV that lists control ID, control owner, artifact types, example file names, and local retention path or Drive link.
- A short playbook (1-2 pages) that describes how to collect runtime log samples and what redaction/PII handling looks like.

Can you send a draft by EOD Monday (May 17)? If you have a canonical example we can use for the audit window, that would speed review.

Also flag any controls you expect will need compensating control justification.

Best,
Julie
Julie Chen
Senior Assessor, Atlas Security
---
Attachment: request-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Chen <julie.chen@atlassecurity.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ - request for control lineage examples and typical artifacts

Hi Julie —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a compact control-lineage matrix (CSV) and a short collection playbook PDF as a starting point. Highlights: 
- The CSV maps control IDs to artifact families (e.g., IAM: IAM policy exports, keystore access logs, KMS rotation docs).
- For runtime telemetry we point assessors to the telemetry-export path in our S3 bucket and include the query used to extract 24-hour samples.
- Tenant isolation: we included the tenancy diagram + keystore scoping sample that audit teams usually request.

Notes / open items: 
1) We flagged three controls where we expect a compensating control explanation (CIS-3.4 / key rotation cadence; CCS-2.1 / ephemeral instance isolation; LOG-5.2 / long-term telemetry retention).
2) We included a recommended sampling window and a suggested redaction checklist for requestors.

I put David on Cc to confirm the log sample query path and retention notes.

Attachments: redwood_control_lineage_matrix_v1.csv, caiq_sample_playbook_v1.pdf

Thanks — happy to walk through tomorrow at 10am PT if you want a quick walkthrough.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Julie / Tessa — quick follow-up after reviewing the matrix: 
- I added an extra column in the CSV for 'example artifact filename' and a short note where we only have ephemeral proofs (screenshots + process doc).
- For the KMS rotation item: David confirmed that rotation policy and last rotation job logs are in the KMS audit stream (link included in Drive).
- I also attached a tiny markdown patch with recommended wording for the compensating control justification — it's included as caiq_response_patch.md.

If Atlas prefers, we can export the telemetry queries as a .sql file for direct ingestion.

Kimberly

Redwood Inference

From: Julie Chen <julie.chen@atlassecurity.com>

Cc: caiq@atlassecurity.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ - request for control lineage examples and typical artifacts

Thanks, team — this is very helpful. The matrix and playbook give our assessors enough to start sampling. A couple of small asks before we close the intake: 
- Can you include one sample runtime log export (anonymized) as an example file for LOG-2.1? If you can't attach data, a sanitized snippet in the Drive link is fine.
- Please confirm the retention period values in the CSV for logs and keystore events.

If you can drop those by EOD Wednesday (May 19) we'll target the CAIQ review next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Julie
